title: Hungary’s communist secret‑police files go online – and a Fidesz MP is named by mistake (Day 178 of the Tisza government)
lede: Budapest finally opens its communist-era files and trims money for cultural and diaspora projects. Prime minister Péter Magyar navigates a minefield where each disclosure risks empowering Fidesz loyalists and unsettling Hungary’s neighbours alike.

title: Robeco and ING launch climate sovereign engagement initiative
lede: The European initiative's initial pilot, supported by IIGCC, focuses on new Dutch government and its legally binding 2030 target.

title: From India to Africa, renewables race ahead but Europe is lagging, IEA report shows
lede: The Iran war has pushed governments from India to sub-Saharan Africa to build more solar and wind, with some regions almost tripling new capacity. But in Europe, that rollout is stalling.

title: EU states back one-year methane delay, but leave door open for more
lede: Member states agreed a one-year delay to the EU’s methane rules, with a built-in option to delay again next year.

title: In the Loop: Awards season, Landerslide and heat losses
lede: Welcome to Responsible Investor’s weekly subscriber-only newsletter! We’d love to hear your feedback, email us at edit@responsible-investor.com.

title: Russians repel attack by Ukrainian ground-robots armed with RPGs, in futuristic assault (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,716)
lede: Ukrainian commander Andriy Biletsky is gambling on mass robot assaults to spare his soldiers’ lives, as Russian troops rush to prove on camera that they can still swat the machines from the sky and fields around Lyman.
